title: Yet true faith is not bare arbitrary assent without solid reasons
source_text: XIX. Illud tamen non minus certum est, veram & legitimam fidem non esse assensum pure arbitrarium, & qui certa & solida ratione destituatur. Res enim quae in Verbo Dei credenda proponuntur, in se quidem sunt obscurae atque inevidentes, sed tamen qui illis eam, quam oportet, fidem adhibent, & convicti sunt Deum esse veracem, & rationibus certis & idoneis moventur, ut credant rebus illis testimonium a Deo perhiberi.
pass_a_gloss: Yet this is no less certain: true and legitimate faith is not a purely arbitrary assent destitute of certain and solid reason. For the things proposed to be believed in God's Word are indeed in themselves obscure and unevident; yet those who give them the faith that is due are convinced that God is truthful, and are moved by certain and fit reasons to believe that testimony is borne by God to those things.
pass_b_english: True faith is not bare arbitrary assent without reason.
Word-objects are obscure in themselves, yet believers are moved by fit reasons that God truly testifies.
